column2: req_desc

Live shelf state.
The server publishes every box's public state and whether sales are open, and pushes each change to every open shelf within 2 seconds.

One winner per number.
Of any number of simultaneous reaches for one box exactly one gets the hold, every other gets the published refusal, and a box never carries two live claims.

Hold ends on its own.
A hold ends at its published edge on the server with no page open and no app code needing to run, and is never extended by a decline, a retry or a repeat request.

Server decides remaining time.
The countdown and match length come only from the server's remaining time, so a wrong device clock or a reload never gains a second.

The held match burns down.
A real 3D match on the held box shortens linearly with the server's remaining time and, at zero, the flame dies, the box darkens on every open shelf and the hold bar shows the published line.

Hold a number journey.
A collector chooses a number on the shelf, sees it held with the time left, can put it back, and sees it return to sale for everyone.

Card checkout with 3-D Secure.
A collector completes checkout through the bank's challenge and ends on an order page showing the card authorised, with the box claimed, a Kill Bill authorisation and one authorisation notice.

Declines, challenge limit and the second try.
Each published decline shows its exact copy and allows another try on the same unextended hold, and a challenge ends at its own limit or the hold's end, whichever comes first.

One attempt key, one authorisation.
One checkout attempt key yields one gateway authorisation and one Kill Bill transaction under double submits and retries, and a repeat returns the first result.

Keyboard-complete checkout.
Every step from shelf to order page, including the bank's challenge, works by keyboard alone with focus kept inside open dialogs and returned to the opener.

Bank transfer order.
A collector choosing bank transfer sees the account details and deadline, the box moves from held to awaiting transfer, and a matching transfer settles the order.

Banking-day deadline.
The transfer deadline falls at the published time on the third banking day after the order in Copenhagen, skipping weekends and the published holidays.

Lapsed, late and wrong transfers.
A lapse releases the box and sends a notice, a late transfer is refunded in full and never reattached, and a wrong amount is sent back with the deadline still running.

Signed gateway callbacks only.
A callback with a bad signature or stale timestamp gets 401 and changes nothing.

Duplicate and reordered callbacks.
A repeated event changes nothing even when delivered concurrently, a late earlier event never moves a payment backwards, and a refund arriving before its capture waits for it.

Authorisation after the hold ended.
An authorisation landing after its hold ended is voided automatically and the buyer sees the published line.

Charged only when confirmed twice.
A collector sees a card as charged only after both the gateway's confirmation and the Kill Bill capture exist.

Packing captures and books.
A packer's `Pack` captures the card, moves the box to packed and then to shipped once the courier is booked, as qualified in Business rules for bank orders.

Failed capture.
A failed capture leaves the box claimed, shows the published copy, alerts the maker and lets the packer try again until the authorisation ends.

Seven-day authorisation.
An uncaptured authorisation is voided by the server at its published edge with nobody watching, the box is released and the maker is alerted.

Paid state and event commit together.
A fulfilment event is written in the same database transaction as the paid state and published afterwards, so a broker outage loses none.

Redelivery changes nothing.
A redelivered event never issues a second certificate, courier booking, receipt, gift notice or webhook.

Fulfilment effects.
A paid order produces a real certificate PDF in storage, a receipt, a signed webhook and, once packed, a courier booking whose tracking code appears in the packer's order list.

Gift notice without prices.
A gift order's recipient gets exactly one notice with the box, plate and message and no price, amount or currency.

Signed events to the charity.
The charity endpoint receives signed, retried `order.paid`, `refund.settled` and `statement.issued` events verifiable with the published secret, and the treasurer sees each one's delivery state as the webhook service reports it.

Private data stays out of copies.
Push alerts, webhook payloads, queue messages and statements carry box numbers and amounts but never a buyer's or recipient's name, email, address or gift message.

Retry and dead-letter.
A failing fulfilment event is retried at the published back-off and lands on the dead-letter list after 3 failed deliveries.

Clearing the list by hand.
A packer sees each dead-lettered event and clears it by retrying it or dismissing it with a note, and the event leaves the dead-letter queue.

Maker push alerts.
A failed capture, an expired authorisation, a dead-lettered event and each downward stock crossing reach the maker's topic within 60 seconds, once each.

Partial refund split.
A partial refund splits into VAT, charity and maker parts by the published rounding at the order's locked rate.

Final refund takes the remainder.
The refund emptying the box takes the exact remainder of each part, so the charity and maker totals reach exactly zero.

Refund settled only when confirmed twice.
A treasurer sees a refund as settled only after both the gateway's confirmation and the Kill Bill refund exist, and a repeat request with one key starts one refund.

Refund journey.
A treasurer finds an order, issues a partial and then a full refund, and sees the ledger view, the buyer's refund notices and the `refund.settled` deliveries follow.

Back on the shelf.
A fully refunded box returns to sale and to public search only after the packer marks it `Back on the shelf`.

Split rate and fees.
Each order's charity and maker shares use the published split at the rate in force at authorisation, and gateway fees come only out of the maker's share and are never returned.

Effective-dated charity rate.
A treasurer sets a new rate only from a future instant, and every earlier order keeps its locked rate on every surface.

Invoice and split agree.
Kill Bill invoice items, stored split lines and statement lines agree to the øre for every order at every moment, as qualified in Business rules.

Monthly charity statement PDF.
A treasurer issues a month's statement as a real PDF with a text layer whose lines and totals match the ledger, stored and downloadable later.

Statement months in Copenhagen.
Sales and refunds post in the Copenhagen calendar month in which they were paid or settled, each refund as a negative line.

Order lookup limit.
Order lookup by reference and email gives one identical refusal for any wrong pair and answers 429 with a wait time after the published number of refused tries.

Certificate download journey.
A collector returning with a reference and email reaches their order and downloads the certificate PDF.

Certificate bytes and cancellation.
An issued certificate keeps identical bytes on every download and, once the order is fully refunded, stops downloading with the published copy.

Typo-tolerant public search.
A reader finds any tale passage or unsold box by number or plate through instant search that tolerates typos, and can jump to the result.

Sold box leaves within seconds.
A sold box leaves public search within 5 seconds and returns only under the published rules.

Staff search and response fields.
Staff can search boxes by recipient, the public index holds no recipient field at all, and every response carries only the fields published for the caller's role.

Safe plate art upload.
Only a maker's PNG or JPEG judged by its content and within the published limits is accepted, and anything else is rejected with published copy.

Plate art persists.
A maker uploads plate art that survives as a file, shows on the box page byte for byte and prints on certificates issued afterwards, leaving earlier certificates unchanged.

Scroll path through seven chapters.
Scroll progress moves the camera along one published path through the seven chapter ranges, in both directions, with state readable from the published scene object, as qualified in Interactions while a box is held.

Striking matches.
A strike by drag, tap, Space or Enter raises a real light and brings up the chapter's vision, the match goes out at its published time except as qualified in Motion and effects for reduced motion and no WebGL, and the grandmother chapter lights the whole bundle.

Sound gate, narration and captions.
A sound question precedes the story, the choice persists, one narration file per chapter ships with the app, and captions always show.

Reduced-motion and no-WebGL story.
Under reduced motion or without WebGL every story, hold and checkout function still works through the published discrete substitutes.

Phone story and checkout.
At 375 px by touch a gift buyer gets the whole story, shelf and gift checkout with a tap to strike and no horizontal overflow.

Shelf by keyboard.
A DOM grid in step with the 3D boxes gives roving focus, arrow keys, Home and End, type-a-number jump, and each box's number, plate and state by name and by shape, and the shelf with a box held has no axe-core violations of the `wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21aa` and `wcag22aa` rule tags.

Published breakpoints.
Each of the three published width bands shows its published shelf columns and staff table layout.

Motion table.
Each interface motion runs at its published length and is readable from the element, and all are instant under reduced motion.

Staff sign-in and roles.
Staff sign in through the identity service with separate roles, only a maker uploads art, only a packer packs and clears, and only a treasurer refunds, sets rates and issues statements.

Working through outages.
With any one of the published services down the app starts, keeps everything else working, answers with the published status and copy, and resumes without a restart when the service returns.

Wintry, kindled look.
The whole product reads as a dark snowbound scene with sparse serif type in which the only warm colour on screen is lit by a match.

The Held Match as a crafted object.
The turn from the story to the shelf and the burning match on the held box read as one continuous, physically lit scene that shows exactly how long the number is held.

Real wiring and media.
The source reads every credential from the environment, calls the real services for every effect, and generates or ships all geometry, art and sound itself from procedural or public-domain sources.
Ship `/app/run.json` with string `install`, `build`, `serve` and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"` at the app root.
List every shipped package with its licence in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`; shipped packages means the production dependency tree (`npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`).
Allow only MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC and 0BSD licences in shipped packages, with OFL for fonts and CC0 or public domain for media.
Use only the datastores and services named in this brief, and add no others.
Leave the provided service configuration and seeded dev credentials unedited.
Keep one narration file per chapter in the repository, and record its offline or public-domain source in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
Load no script, font, model, sound or image from another origin at run time.
